226.t: Chicago bands: Fambrough, Earle Warren and his own group at Joe's Deluxe
226.s: He worked with Tony Fambrough, Earle Warren's band at Joe Louis's club, Boyd Atkins and led his own group.
226.ch: Depression-era Chicago: jobs, marriage, first bands
226.q: There was Tony Fambrough. There was – I worked with – Earle Warren had a band that worked in a club that Joe Louis fronted. That was with Earle Warren’s band. Then there was another group that I worked with in a nightclub setting.

226.t: Working with Boyd Atkins and leading his own group
226.s: He alternated between leading and sideman jobs with Boyd Atkins and Earle Warren.
226.ch: Depression-era Chicago: jobs, marriage, first bands
226.q: At times I had my own group. At other times I worked with other groups. Boyd Atkins, I worked with for nightclubs on the south side of Chicago, and as I said, Earle Warren at the Joe Louis club on the south side in Chicago. Then I had my own group that I worked at Joe’s Deluxe.

237.t: Sorting out the chronology and when he reached Kansas City
237.s: Goodwin and Smith untangle Lovett's order of bands, Thamon Hayes and George Lee, and settle that he arrived by 1922-23.
237.q: I'm trying to think, I think I'm getting it straight now. It was so far back.

237.t: Years with George and Julia Lee, then Thamon Hayes
237.s: He was with George Lee about five years from 1925-26, then joined Thamon Hayes around 1931 for about three years, with two Chicago trips.
237.q: Let's see, I think that was about in the twenties, around about '25 or '26.

264.t: Dating the Petit photo to about 1920-21
264.s: Russell and Zardis settle that the photo dates to around 1920-21, noting Edmund Hall's estimate.
264.q: That's around 20 or 21. It's around that time between 19 and 21. Yeah. That's all. Well what time, they got 20 on there.

22.t: La Rocca corrects his contract dates; end of Averty's letter
22.s: La Rocca says the second set of dates is right, and the interviewer reads the rest of the letter.
22.ch: Averty's letters and Tom Brown's claims
22.q: june 3rd 1916 those are the correct dates after i looked up my books the others was given from memory and that will show you about anybody that gives from memory can remember all the things that's happened in the exact dates and times of what has transpired after 40 years this man mr abety is…

456.t: Trying to pin down the dates of his moves
456.s: Allen and Mazzari struggle over what year he returned to the US and came to New Orleans; Mazzari says about 1938 and about 1948 and admits he is bad with dates.
456.q: Uh, thirty-nine, no, thirty-eight. Thirty-eight. Something like that.

248.t: Dawson's list of bands and dance halls, 1904 onward
248.s: Dawson reads off his career: dance halls and bandleaders from 1904 (Parker's, Anderson's, Phillips', Oliver, Kelly, Rene); with Manetta he corrects the dates for Puclos and Parker's.
248.q: I started the playing in 1904 at Hugh Cloth's Dance Hall with O'Neill Lavish's Band, Franklin Y. Iberville. 1905 at Tom Anderson with Moran's Band, Basin and Iberville. 1907 at Harry Parker's Dance Hall, Dawson and Minetta's Band, Franklin between Iberville and Benwood. 1910 at Biller Phillips…

708.t: Working at the Cotton Club on Blue Island
708.s: She worked briefly at the Cotton Club on Blue Island and cannot recall which band was there.
708.q: Uh-huh. Then, when I left there, I went to, to where I worked at the, uh, Cotton Club for a while. Uh, which one? Uh, uh, uh, on Blue Island. Yes. Over there. And, uh...

136.t: Correcting the chronology of the Mingus period
136.s: Brown and she sort out the dates and conclude her Mingus period came after 1964, probably after 1966.
136.ch: New York clubs, marriage and tours
136.q: So the Mingus…. When Mingus asked me to join, I was really alone and struggling. Barely paying the rent. And uh, my daughter was with my sister in Japan, and—I think she‟d just started kindergarten or something, kindergarten or grammar school, I‟m not quite sure.

66.t: Sorting out the chronology: Chicago, the Pearl and joining the band
66.s: She and the interviewer untangle the order: Chicago recording was the band's start, the Pearl came before, and the Pearl is where she became a regular member.
66.ch: Memphis, Oklahoma, the Kirk band and Kansas City
66.q: Yes... When we went to Chicago to record for Jack Kapp, that was the beginning of the success of the band and then later on Jack Kapp moved to New York and became Decca. I guess that was less than a year and Joe Glaser came out of Chicago. Then when they had those hits, that was in '33 or '34.

96.t: Husk O'Hare's Wolverines under his direction; Des Moines
96.s: Dick Voynow becomes an A and R man and gives him the Wolverines name; he books the Austin High men through Husk O'Hare, playing Des Moines.
96.q: We did that vaudeville for a little bit. I had gotten the Austin Highschool Gang then. By that time I had Davey Tough, I had Dick Voynow get Davey Tough on drums, my brother on guitar and banjo. My brother-in-law, Jim Lanigan on string bass and Bud Freeman on tenor saxophone and Teschemaker on…

455.s: Hinton and Budd pin down which year they are discussing.
455.ch: Kansas City, Basie, Prez and Booker Pittman
455.q: stranded, you see. This story kind of jumps a little bit, because a certain question'll come up and I get carried away on it.
